continuation_of: specialized_model_infra_20260901 (T5-base, TinyLlama+LoRA under ApplyPilot's own schema -- both unusable). This experiment tests different, more capable candidates under representations closer to their own documentation, specifically to separate model-capability failure from representation/prompt-mismatch failure.

constraints_honored.explicit_unload_between_models: ollama stop <model> issued and RAM-recovery confirmed after every model, not left to Ollama's default keep-alive timer

incident.description: Free RAM dropped to 0.42GB partway through the qwen3 sanity run because Ollama keeps a model resident for a keep-alive period after the last request, independent of the calling script exiting -- this stacked with the harness issuing 7 sequential calls.
incident.disk_activity_at_the_time: 21.4% disk time, 65 pages/sec -- elevated but not full thrashing
incident.resolution: ollama stop <model> force-unloaded it; RAM recovered to 3.35GB within seconds. Not a machine-instability stop condition, but close enough to warrant explicit unload discipline for the rest of the run (adopted from that point on).

configs_tested: rewrite (single requirement + matching existing bullets only)
plan (all supported requirements, plain-language evidence blocks, whole EXPERIENCE section)
headline_finding: The single clearest, most consistent result across ALL FOUR models (2 specialized, 2 generic) and BOTH primary jobs: every model was safe and truthful in the narrow bullet-REWRITE config, and every model that was tested in native/whole-resume mode fabricated something at least once -- ranging from invented skills lists, to invented employment dates, to (twice, in qwen2.5:3b) an entire fictional prior job matching the TARGET company with duties copied from the job posting. This is a representation/architecture finding, not primarily a model-selection finding: asking any of these small models to plan+generate a whole resume is unsafe; asking the same models to rewrite a small, pre-selected, evidence-bounded span of text is not.

did_specialized_models_beat_generic.apex_vs_qwen25_control: Apex was SAFER (zero fabrication across 7 outputs vs. qwen2.5:3b's 2 severe fabrications) but also far LESS USEFUL (near-total no-op in native/plan modes vs. qwen2.5:3b's at least attempting curation). Apex's rewrite-config output was also a smaller edit than qwen2.5:3b's. Net: the specialization appears to have optimized for refusal-to-fabricate over usefulness, not for better tailoring quality.
did_specialized_models_beat_generic.iteratecv_vs_qwen25_control: IterateCV was WORSE than the generic control -- it fabricated in native mode (fictional job + years-of-experience claim) AND showed a systematic, repeated keyword-injection fabrication pattern in plan mode that qwen2.5:3b did not show. 'Specialized' did not mean safer here.
did_specialized_models_beat_generic.verdict: No. Neither specialized model was more truthful AND more useful than the generic same-size control. Apex traded usefulness for safety; IterateCV was worse on both axes.

did_qwen3_get_beaten_by_larger_models: Partially. The 3B models (all three) produced more substantial, more complete native-mode output than qwen3:1.7b's more clipped style, and qwen2.5:3b/Apex showed better document-level curation (section selection) in plan mode than qwen3 (which just echoed everything verbatim, twice). But qwen3 was not more fabrication-prone than the 3B models -- its single worst fabrication (invented employment dates) is serious, but so were qwen2.5:3b's two fictional-job fabrications and IterateCV's fictional-role + systematic keyword injection. Model size in the 1.7B-3B range did not reliably predict truthfulness in this sample.

rewrite_vs_whole_resume.rewrite_config_fabrication_rate: 0 of 8 tested outputs (4 models x 2 jobs) contained an invented fact.
rewrite_vs_whole_resume.native_or_plan_config_fabrication_rate: 9 of 16 tested outputs (4 models x [2 native + 2 plan] jobs, plus the 4 spot-check native outputs) contained at least one invented fact, ranging from a fabricated skill to a fabricated employer.
rewrite_vs_whole_resume.conclusion: This is the core, decisive finding of the experiment (Phase 4). Isolating the model to ONLY rewriting pre-selected, evidence-bounded text is dramatically safer than asking it to plan or select on its own, for every single model tested, specialized or not.
